sources.entry: Rebind - Open-source tool for remapping keys, mouse buttons and trackpad gestures to shortcuts and system actions. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Blinks44/rebind) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Rebind
summary.one_liner: Rebind is a free, open-source native macOS app that remaps keyboard keys, mouse buttons and trackpad gestures to shortcuts and system actions from the menu bar.
use_cases: remap a mouse side button to Mission Control or Spaces switching
bind a function key to play/pause or media actions
snap windows to halves with a keyboard shortcut
use different key bindings for work and games via profiles
add trackpad tap gestures for actions not built into macOS
reverse mouse scrolling direction separately for vertical and horizontal
summary.what_it_does: Rebind lets you assign actions to keys, mouse buttons, built-in trackpad, Magic Trackpad and Magic Mouse inputs, with bindings firing on press, double press or hold (hold time set per binding). Mouse buttons can trigger different actions per direction when held and moved, and a modifier with the scroll wheel can switch Spaces. It offers 93 actions including window snapping, Spaces, sound control, opening apps, typing saved text and running Apple Shortcuts. Profiles (up to 20) can hold bindings that apply to all apps or only the app in front, and an emergency pause shortcut disables all bindings. Per-mouse settings cover Logitech pointer speed, DPI, SmartShift and scroll options for any mouse.
notable: Open source, native Mac app that runs from the menu bar
Per-device and per-app bindings with profiles switchable by key or menu bar
Press, double-press and hold triggers, including a hold binding that also sends a short-tap shortcut
Does not record typed input; only network request is a daily update check that can be disabled
caveats: Trackpad and Magic Mouse gestures are experimental and rely on an undocumented macOS interface that may change with system updates
Not notarized by Apple yet, so the first launch needs a Terminal command or Privacy & Security override
